headline: Search the board once against a trie of all words
statement: Return all distinct dictionary words that can be formed on board by horizontal or vertical adjacent cells, without using a cell twice within one word. Return words in any order.
constraints: Words are distinct lowercase strings of length 1..10
Board cells are lowercase English letters.
intuition: Many words share their first letters. Store those shared beginnings in a trie, then walk the board while following trie paths. If a board path does not match any stored beginning, stop that search immediately. This avoids searching the entire board separately for every word.
approach: Insert each word into a nested dictionary trie and store the complete word at its terminal node.
Start DFS from each board cell; follow the corresponding trie edge only if present.
Emit and remove terminal words to avoid duplicates across paths.
Mark the cell during neighbor recursion and restore it afterward; prune exhausted trie branches.
correctness: The trie node reached by a board path represents exactly its spelled prefix. Missing edges cannot lead to dictionary words. Each matching terminal emits a valid path word, and removing its terminal prevents duplicate emission. All legal board paths are considered until their prefix becomes impossible, so every obtainable word is found.
bruteForce: Run Word Search independently for every word, repeating common-prefix searches.

complexity.explanation: D is the total number of dictionary characters and L is the maximum word length. A start has at most four next choices; subsequent path cells have at most three because the previous cell is unavailable. Trie construction costs O(D), and recursion uses O(L) space in addition to the trie.

pitfalls: Remove the terminal marker after reporting a word, but continue for longer words sharing its prefix.
Keep path visitation separate from dictionary prefix state.
Restore the board after exploring a branch.
